editorial.headline: Other Animal Breeding With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01499 covers the breeding and cultivation of animals such as guinea pigs, dogs, cats, worms, and crickets, with PMA access open nationally and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01499 is for the cultivation and breeding of other animals: a deliberately practical category for activities that do not sit inside the more familiar livestock boxes. The slim record names guinea pigs, dogs, cats, worms, and crickets as examples, and it frames the business purpose broadly: producing breeding stock, meat, skins, and other outputs. In plain English, this is an animal-rearing and breeding activity where the commercial product may be the animal itself, its offspring, or material derived from the animal.

The code is open across the full business-size spectrum. A founder can read the scale field cleanly: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all listed as eligible scales. That matters because this is not only a backyard or smallholder classification; the record also accommodates larger operators. The scope is still bounded by the activity itself: breeding and cultivating the listed kinds of animals, or comparable “other animals,” for the outputs stated in the record.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. There is no partial cap in the slim record, so the editorial reading is not “open but limited”; it is nationally open to full foreign ownership as recorded. That does not create any extra licence, tax, capital, or timeline rule here. It only states the investment-access position provided by the record.

The Bali picture is also unusually clear. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this record is not blocked for Bali. Its L4 Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. In practical editorial terms: a foreign investor looking at this activity is not facing a Bali PMA registration block under the moratorium described in the record.
